ideas.pitch: An AI-assisted code review and telemetry logger that flags suspicious git diffs, deliberate syntax obfuscation, and malicious comment sabotage during team coding challenges.
ideas.problem_statement: Tech Mafia: Innocents must complete technical challenges while identifying Mafia members who try to slow down, mislead, and sabotage their team.
ideas.title: SabotageSleuth
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly targets the core game mechanic of Tech Mafia by helping Innocents detect who is sabotaging the codebase, aligning with patterns from winning debugging agents like bobthebuilder.

ideas.pitch: A controlled playground and prompt-logging wrapper designed to catch Mafia members who inject hallucination-inducing or destructive prompts into shared AI coding assistants.
ideas.problem_statement: Tech Mafia: Technical social deduction game combining coding, debugging, AI prompting, logical reasoning, and strategy.
ideas.title: PromptDeceiver
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages the specific inclusion of AI prompting in the hackathon description, giving Innocents an audit trail of who prompted what and when.

ideas.pitch: A micro-IDE extension that records granular keystroke and test-running provenance to provide incontrovertible proof of innocence or guilt during team code reviews.
ideas.problem_statement: Tech Mafia: Across the first two rounds, participants must balance performing well and figuring out who they can trust before the team elimination vote.
ideas.title: AlibiCode
ideas.why_it_could_win: Solves the exact social deduction pain point of 'he said, she said' accusations in technical rounds with hard telemetry data, matching the functional demo standard of codeboost.

ideas.pitch: A real-time team analytics overlay that tracks test suite execution times, commit failure frequencies, and suspicious code reverts to quantify individual sabotage risk.
ideas.problem_statement: Tech Mafia: The Innocents must work together to complete technical challenges as efficiently as possible while Mafia members mislead and sabotage.
ideas.title: DeceptionDashboard
ideas.why_it_could_win: Provides a live, working dashboard that judges and players can look at during Round 1 and 2 to make data-backed social deduction accusations.

ideas.pitch: A speed-coding and rapid-debugging micro-game simulating Round 3's individual survival challenges to help players train for the final elimination round.
ideas.problem_statement: Tech Mafia: Round 3 eliminates the team element completely, requiring participants to compete individually through a series of technical and mental challenges.
ideas.title: RoundThreeTrainer
ideas.why_it_could_win: Anticipates the final round format of the event, appealing directly to the organizers and participants who need to practice for individual survival.
